title_original: סיפור בשלבים (Hebrew-original game by יצירה (Yetzira), box number #5278; no foreign original found)
israeli_distributor: יצירה (Yetzira), Hebrew-original game sold under the 'יצירה' brand by Israeli toy shops and kindergarten suppliers; no separate importer named on the pages read

official_age.text: Box prints '+2' under the Yetzira logo (read in the 2022 Hebrew packshot). Retailers write 'לגילאי 2-5' (Moran Toys, Amigo, Daniela Gan), 'גיל 2-5' (Nir Galim) and 'משחק לגילאי 2+' (Center Toys). Minimum 2. No Yetzira product page was found, so the box is the official source.
official_age.source: Yetzira box packshot (age printed on the box front), as published on Amigo's product page; upper age 5 from the retailers' text

popularity_signals.description: Displayed position 232 of 1659 in the Center Toys board-games category ('משחקי קופסא') with the store's own sort 'למיין לפי פופולריות'. Page 10 of 70 read on 2026-10-14 ('מציג 217–240 מתוך 1659'), products counted in page order, 24 per page. The site runs WooCommerce, whose popularity sort orders by recorded sales; the store does not state a time window. 232 of 1659 is 14 percent, outside the top 20 and the top 10 percent, so this is a supporting signal only.

Listed by several independent Israeli sellers, pages opened 2026-10-14: Center Toys (in stock), Moran Toys (in stock, '2 במלאי'), Amigo (in stock), and two kindergarten equipment suppliers, Nir Galim ('ציוד לגני ילדים ובתי ספר', page markup InStock, price on quote) and Daniela Gan Rehovot ('ציוד לגני ילדים', 'סיפור בשלבים מבית יצירה'). Being carried by kindergarten suppliers suggests use in Israeli kindergartens, but that is an inference, not a stated fact.
popularity_signals.quote: סיפור בשלבים - תעשיות ניר גלים - ציוד לגני ילדים ובתי ספר

popularity_reasoning: No strong signal. Two supporting signals from two groups: the Center Toys popularity sort (232 of 1659, 14 percent) and five independent Israeli sellers, three of them showing stock today and two of them kindergarten suppliers. popular_in_israel through the two-signal route. Stronger than Zingo's ranking, but still not a top-10-percent position.
developmental_relevance: Twelve illustrated three-step stories ('מה קודם למה? 12 סיפורים מאוירים בשלושה שלבים!'): the children put three pieces in order and then have a reason to tell what happens first, next and at the end. The box itself says 'משחק לפיתוח תפיסה חזותית ולהעשרת אוצר המילים!'. Telling each three-step story aloud is a chance to practise sentences of four or more words (CDC 4 year milestone) and back-and-forth talk when the parent asks 'Why?' and 'How?' (CDC 5 year milestone and tip); KidsHealth names talking and asking questions among everyday ways to support vocabulary at 4 to 5. The talk comes from the way it is played together: the pieces alone are a sequencing puzzle.
parent_tip_source: Our suggestion, from the box's 'מה קודם למה?' idea: after the children lay out the three pieces, ask them to tell the story out loud with 'קודם... אחר כך... בסוף...', then ask 'למה?' and 'איך?' about one picture (CDC 5 year tip: help a child expand answers by asking 'Why?' and 'How?'). For older children, mix two stories and let them sort and tell both.

image.rights_note: The 2022 Hebrew box packshot (file name 5278_heb_2022, the same file Zrizi uses, so probably the maker's own image) on Amigo's product page; the box shows the Yetzira logo, '+2' and '#5278'. No watermark. No press kit or media licence seen. Center Toys hosts a smaller 477x523 copy of the same box.

limitations: Popularity rests on supporting signals only (a store popularity sort of unknown window plus several sellers). The official age is low (box +2, shops 2-5), so it may feel easy for older 5 year olds; the stage minimum 4 is above the official minimum, which the rules allow. The mechanism is a three-piece sequencing puzzle: the word play depends on the parent asking the children to tell the story, which the copy must say. No Yetzira website was found, so maker details come from the box and retailer pages. Image from a retailer page, rights unverified. Different type from the headband guessing and pairs memory games.

popularity_signals.description: Listed by six independent Israeli sellers, pages opened 2026-10-14: Mindx, Bug, Endendino, Center Toys and Toyland (all in stock by page text or markup) and Ganshop ('מרכז לגנים ולתלמיד', 119.90, stock not stated).

A Hebrew edition exists: the box reads 'בינגו עם זינג', Endendino says the boards are in Hebrew ('הלוחות בשפה העברית') and Mindx lists Hebrew rules ('חוברת הוראות בעברית'). Mindx names the brand behind it as Sahek Na and describes it as one of Israel's veteran leading games importers (Ravensburger, Educa). That description comes from a retailer's brand note, not from Sahek Na itself.
popularity_signals.quote: חברת "שחק נא" היא מהיבואניות הוותיקות והמובילות של משחקי קופסה ופנאי בישראל.

popularity_signals.description: Displayed position 589 of 1659 in the Center Toys board-games category with the store's own sort 'למיין לפי פופולריות' (WooCommerce popularity sort, recorded sales, window not stated). Page 25 of 70 read on 2026-10-14 ('מציג 577–600 מתוך 1659'), counted in page order. 589 of 1659 is 36 percent: a weak supporting signal only.

popularity_reasoning: No strong signal. Supporting signals from three groups: six Israeli sellers, a Hebrew edition from an importer a retailer calls veteran and leading, and a low store popularity position (589 of 1659). popular_in_israel through the two-signal route, but the evidence is broad availability more than proven sales; the weaker of the two on popularity.
developmental_relevance: A picture bingo for 2 to 6 players: the Zingo Zinger slides out two picture tiles at a time and players match them to their Hebrew boards. In Mindx's Hebrew rules the first player to spot a match says the picture's name aloud before taking it ('השחקן הראשון שמזהה התאמה קורא בקול את שם התמונה ולוקח את האריח'), so every tile is a reason to name a thing out loud. Sits next to KidsHealth's 'playing word games' for vocabulary at 4 to 5 and CDC's 4 year tip to play matching games. Naming single pictures is an opportunity to practise vocabulary; sentences come from the parent adding talk.
parent_tip_source: Our suggestion, from the rule that the player who spots a match names the picture aloud: say every revealed picture together, then let the one who takes it add one sentence about it ('הכלב ישן על השטיח'), which practises sentences of four or more words (CDC 4 year milestone); with younger players, play without the race and let each child name and place in turn.

image.rights_note: Packshot of the Israeli Hebrew-edition box ('Zingo! בינגו עם זינג', 'גילאים 4 ומעלה') on Mindx's product page, on a white background. No watermark. The box carries foreign award seals (TOTY 2009 and others), which are not Israeli signals. No press kit or media licence seen.

limitations: Popularity rests on supporting signals only and the store ranking is low (589 of 1659). Bug and Endendino show the same barcode (019275077006); Endendino and Mindx describe Hebrew boards and rules, Bug's page does not state the language, so every listing being the Hebrew edition is not confirmed. The importer's description comes from a retailer's brand note. ThinkFun's official page could not be read (redirect then 403), so the age comes from the Hebrew box and retailer text. The race to grab tiles can frustrate some 4 year olds. Matching is part of the play, but the mechanism (bingo with a dispenser and naming aloud) differs from the pairs memory game already in the carousel.
